correctness.rationale: The finite claim is a complete exhaustive theorem: all \(2^n\) binary words and every unordered pair are enumerated for each \(4\le n\le9\); eligibility is checked both by disjoint \(\mathcal D_2\) balls and independently by longest-common-subsequence length; every \(\mathcal D_3\) intersection is counted. The embedded verifier reproduces the six maxima, witnesses, \(174216\) pair checks, and \(94949\) eligible pairs. The tail \(20\) uses the actual stated hypotheses of arXiv:2111.04255v1 Theorem 4 and Proposition 5/Corollary 6, with \(\ell=t=3\), so no finite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: This closes the entire preasymptotic interval for the first diagonal deletion-reconstruction case beyond the previously exact \(\ell\in\{1,2\}\) regimes. The invariant directly equals the worst-case number of ambiguous distinct reads; hence the profile gives the exact unique-reconstruction requirement \(N(n,3,3)+1\) at every admissible length. The strict value \(N(9,3,3)=15<20\) also proves that the published sufficient stabilization threshold \(n=10\) is sharp for \(t=3\).
